subject: Clarifying which artifacts Redwood keeps by default — requests vs outputs
messages:
From: Erin Lawson <erin.lawson@greenfieldhealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick question on what Redwood stores by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Naomi —

Quick question as we finish our security review: can you clarify exactly what Redwood keeps by default for a hosted customer? In particular we need to understand

- whether raw user requests (the text the user typed) are stored by default;
- how model responses (generated text) are treated (are those kept longer or considered derivatives); and
- any distinctions you make for streaming sessions, function/tool outputs, or embeddings.

We're documenting the default retention and what we can ask to change (e.g., zero retention for PII). A short plain-language summary + any links to a matrix would be helpful.

Thanks —
Erin
Erin Lawson
Security & Procurement
Greenfield Health

---
Attachment: retention-ask-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Erin Lawson <erin.lawson@greenfieldhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 8 Oct 2025 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood stores by default (requests vs outputs)

Hi Erin —

Thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise, actionable summary of our default behavior and the configuration options we offer. I kept this high-level first, then Karthik has added a few technical caveats.

Summary (plain language):
- User requests / prompts: by default we retain text inputs for 30 days in the hosted control plane for troubleshooting and quality monitoring. Inputs are treatable as "requests" (raw user-supplied content).
- Model outputs (generated completions / responses): stored by default for 90 days; treated as "derivatives"/"outputs" (used for model evals, debug, and regressions).
- Streaming sessions: we store the final produced output and a compacted transcript (not every intermediate token) using the same retention windows above.
- Function/tool outputs (attachments, tool results): treated as outputs; retention depends on type (small JSON/text = 90 days, large binary artifacts we surface as attachment stubs and reference their retention in the console).
- Embeddings / vectors: we do not store raw vectors in the hosted control plane by default for analytics; persisted embeddings are opt-in via the embeddings-api+storage feature (customers control TTL).

Options we can provide for Greenfield Health:
- Zero-retention profile: we can enable a policy that purges requests immediately (TTL=0) after successful delivery; outputs can also be configured to be purged on the same schedule. This is typically a special flag set on the customer's org.
- Regional residency: data can be pinned to a US region; for EU residency we use EU-only storage helplines.
- Redaction: we offer outbound redaction hooks and client-side SDK helpers (we can share examples).

Attached is a simple matrix and a short runbook (PDF) that summarizes the default windows and where to change them in the Console. If you want, Karthik can follow up with the API/delete-runbook snippet and the compliance checklist.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Director, Solution Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-retention-matrix.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Erin Lawson <erin.lawson@greenfieldhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Oct 2025 02:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick question on what Redwood stores by default (requests vs outputs)

Looping in a couple technical details from the runtime/infra side — Erin, feel free to skip the dense bits.

Technical clarifications / caveats:
- "Request" vs "Derived output": we use those two labels internally. Requests are the raw bytes sent by the customer API call; derivatives include model logits, token-level traces, and final outputs. Some internal observability traces (error telemetry) are persisted for 180 days by default for platform health — those traces are NOT correlated to customer content and are hashed/metadata-only.
- KV cache / session material: transient KV cache used for in-flight sessions lives on serving nodes and is evicted per session; we do not persist KV cache to durable control-plane storage unless a customer enables session-archival.
- Streams: for streaming responses we write a compact transcript that omits very short-lived intermediate states (we keep the final stable output + timestamped deltas).
- Deletion path and audit: we provide a Delete API (DELETE /v1/orgs/{org_id}/artifacts) that accepts filters (type=requests|outputs, before=ISO, tag=project). Deletions surface as a retention job; a runbook with examples is attached. Deletion does not immediately zero out block storage but tombstones records and triggers background purge (typical completion within 48–72 hours).
- Opt-out/zero-ttl: when enabled we still log a small immutable audit record (UUID, timestamp, org-id) to meet operational audit requirements; that record does not contain user content.
- Regulatory exceptions: for customers who require a contractual data retention shorter than platform minimal windows we offer Dedicated/Private deployment options with SLA-backed retention guarantees.

I'll paste a snippet from the runbook if you want CLI/API commands; otherwise happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the console toggles.

-Karthik

Attachments: runbook-delete-api-snippets.txt
